The '''2024–25 Czech First League''', known as the '''[[Czech First League|Chance Liga]]''' for sponsorship reasons, was the 32nd season of the [[Czech Republic]]'s top-tier [[association football|football]] for professional clubs since its establishment in 1993. [[AC Sparta Prague|Sparta Prague]] were the reigning champions. The first half of the season had 19 rounds, starting in July 2024 and finishing in December. The second half commenced in February 2025. The season ended on 25 May 2025 with two extra play-out fixtures on 29 May and 1 June 2025.<ref name=idnes>{{cite web |title=Příští sezona fotbalové ligy začne 20. července, jaro o týden dřív než dosud|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/prvni-liga/fortuna-liga-sezona-2024-2025-terminy-reditel-lfa-tomas-barta.A231128_151615_fotbal_min|website=iDNES.cz|language=cs|date=2023-11-28|publisher=Mafra}}</ref>

==Format==
From the start of the 2024–25 season, the league became known as the "Chance Liga" after its new main sponsor, Chance betting office.<ref>{{cite web |title=Čtvrt miliardy za jméno fotbalové ligy. Tendr vyhrála sázková kancelář Chance|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/prvni-liga/chance-liga-tendr-vyberove-rizeni-partner-sponzor-lfa.A240417_094820_fotbal_min|website=iDNES.cz|language=cs|date=2024-04-17|publisher=Mafra}}</ref> The general season format was unchanged from the last season; the 16 clubs played each other home and away, until the league was split up in championship, play-off and relegation groups. The lowest-ranked team were relegated directly to the second league, and the two teams positioned 14th and 15th played a play-out with two teams from the second league positioned 2nd and 3rd in a home and away format. The change was the cancellation of the Conference League play-off final between the team finishing 5th and the team winning the play-off group. The winner of the middle group (i.e. the team placed 7th) only received a financial bonus.<ref>{{cite web |title=Velká změna v lize! Prostřední skupina nadstavby už nebude motivována evropskými poháry, nýbrž pouhou finanční injekcí|url=https://www.ruik.cz/velka-zmena-v-lize-prostredni-skupina-nadstavby-uz-nebude-motivovana-evropskymi-pohary-nybrz-pouhou-financni-injekci/|website=ruik.cz|language=cs|date=2024-06-21}}</ref>

This is the seventh season to use [[Video assistant referee|VAR]], featuring it in all matches played. The VAR central workplace in the [[Michle]] district of Prague was used for the first time. VAR had offside line technology available for the first time.<ref>{{cite web |title=VAR na jednom místě. Sudí ve fotbalové lize od léta uvítají novinku|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/prvni-liga/fortuna-liga-sezona-2024-2025-terminy-reditel-lfa-tomas-barta.A231128_151615_fotbal_min|website=iDNES.cz|language=cs|date=2024-06-13|publisher=Mafra}}</ref>

In the 2024–25 season, three new rules were introduced. The first is the ability for teams to use a sixth substitution if there is a head injury or concussion. Secondly, the punishment for a player in a situation where that player spoils a clear scoring opportunity with his hand was changed, and only a yellow card was awarded instead of a red card. Finally, the assessment of premature running of players into the penalty area during a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] also changed.<ref>{{cite web |title=Z trabantu do škodovky. Šéf sudích Kovařík o změnách i inspiraci z Eura|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/prvni-liga/predseda-komise-rozhodcich-libor-kovarik-rozhovor-novinky-pravidla.A240711_220103_fotbal_duff|work=iDNES.cz|language=cs|date=2024-07-12|publisher=Mafra}}</ref>

Other changes concern the dates of matches, which is partly due to the new format of the European competitions. The spring part started a week earlier than in previous years (on 1 February) and the exact dates of the matches were determined further in advance than three weeks, as has been the case so far.<ref name=idnes/>

==Events==
SK Dynamo České Budějovice became the first team in the history of the Czech First League to not win any match in the regular season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rekordní pád Dynama. Čekání na nového majitele i licenci, veletoče trenérů|url=https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/fotbal-chance-liga/460965/rekordni-pad-dynama-cekani-na-noveho-majitele-i-licenci-veletoce-treneru.html|website=isport.blesk.cz|language=cs|date=2025-04-26|access-date=2025-05-18}}</ref> After continuing the run in the season-ending relegation group, in which they picked up a solitary point, the club finished their 35-game season without winning (29 losses, 6 draws).<ref>{{cite news |title=Dukla - Č. Budějovice 2:1, Jihočeši ani v posledním zápase nedokázali zvítězit |url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/prvni-liga/chance-liga-skupina-o-udrzeni-dukla-budejovice.A250523_161254_fotbal_tals |access-date=28 May 2025 |work=idnes.cz |publisher=Mafra |date=25 May 2025 |language=cs}}</ref>

===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
A total of sixteen teams contest the league, including 15 sides from the 2023–24 season and the winner of last season's second league.

;Team promoted to Czech First League
After being relegated in the [[2018–19 Czech First League|2018–19]] season, [[FK Dukla Prague]] returned to Czech First League as the champion of the [[2023–24 Czech National Football League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Fotbalisté pražské Dukly se vrací do nejvyšší soutěže, dvě kola před koncem ligy slaví přímý postup|url=https://www.irozhlas.cz/sport/fotbal/fotbal-dukla-praha-rada_2405121918_tpk|website=[[Czech Radio]]|language=cs|date=2024-05-12}}</ref>

;Teams relegated from Czech First League
The lowest positioned team from the [[2023–24 Czech First League|last season]], [[FC Zlín]], was relegated to the Czech National Football League.
